questions.verification_notes: Verified directly from NHGRI Sequencing_Cost_Data_Table_May2022.xls, sheet Data Table: the row dated 2022-05-31 reports Cost per Genome of approximately $524.624684, rounded to $525. The source methodology includes production labor, supplies, amortized sequencing equipment and initial processing; it excludes downstream analysis and other non-production activities. Genome cost is an estimate using a human-sized 3,000 Mb genome and platform-specific coverage assumptions. Replaces the undated $200 manufacturer minimum with an explicitly dated NIH-funded-center production benchmark. This is the May observation, not an annual average or a present-day retail price.

expected.question_text: What is the cost in USD to sequence a full human genome?
expected.answer_context: As of 2025, sequencing giant Illumina can achieve whole genome sequencing for as little as $200 using their NovaSeq X series platform. This represents a dramatic decrease from $100 million in 2001 and $1 million in 2007. The cost continues to decline as technology advances toward the goal of a $100 genome.

questions.question_text: In May 2022, approximately what did it cost in US dollars to sequence a human genome at NIH-funded centers?
questions.measure_definition: NHGRI estimated production cost per human-sized genome, in US dollars, rounded to the nearest dollar. Derived from center cost-accounting data and coverage assumptions, not a retail or clinical test price.
questions.source_name: NHGRI — DNA Sequencing Costs; NHGRI — May 2022 data table
questions.answer_context: This benchmark includes sequencing labor, supplies and equipment costs. It excludes downstream interpretation and other non-production work, so a clinical test can cost more. Lower sequencing costs help make larger genomic studies possible.
